hotspots.title: Lecture hall
hotspots.text: The lecturer explains how sentences are built and how people actually learn a second language, step by step.
hotspots.fact: You study how language works and how learners acquire it.

hotspots.title: Language lab
hotspots.text: With headphones on, you practise pronunciation, listen to native speakers, and record yourself to hear what to improve.
hotspots.fact: Teachers practise the skills they will teach.

hotspots.title: Lesson studio
hotspots.text: You design a short lesson: a goal, an activity, and simple materials that keep a class interested.
hotspots.fact: Planning a lesson is a skill you practise repeatedly.

hotspots.title: Microteaching room
hotspots.text: You teach ten minutes to classmates who act as students, then they tell you what worked and what did not.
hotspots.fact: Feedback from peers is a regular part of training.

hotspots.title: School
hotspots.text: You assist a real teacher in a classroom, handle a small group, and see what a school day feels like.
hotspots.fact: Graduates teach in schools and language centers, among other paths.
